challenges.name: mutation-testing-quiz
challenges.title: What does the mutation report say?
challenges.description: A surviving mutant in CodeDev's pricing rule next to a 100% coverage report, and the summary of a mutation run checked against a CI gate.

questions.explanation: True. The mutant changes >= to >, which only behaves differently for 7 itself. A streak of 3 takes the second branch under both versions and a streak of 12 takes the first under both, so both tests pass on the mutant and it survives. With the mutant, streakBonus(7) returns 7 * 5 = 35 instead of 50, so a test expecting 50 fails and the mutant is killed. Coverage is 100% because both branches run, but coverage only says the lines were executed, not that a test would notice if they were wrong. The misconception is that full branch coverage means the boundary is tested.

questions.question:
Mutation run for src/enrollments (80 mutants):
  killed 40 · timeout 5 · survived 10 · no coverage 5 · compile error 20 · ignored 0

CI gate: fail the build when the mutation score is below 70, with the score defined as StrykerJS documents it.

Statement: "The mutation score is 50% (40 of the 80 mutants were killed), so this run fails the gate."
questions.explanation: False. With the StrykerJS definition, a mutant is detected when it is killed or times out (45 here), undetected when it survives or no test covers it (15), and the valid mutants are detected plus undetected (60). Compile errors are invalid mutants: the changed code never ran, so they say nothing about the tests and are left out, like ignored mutants. The score is 45 / 60 = 75%, which passes a gate of 70. The misconception is that the score is killed divided by all mutants generated; that undercounts timeouts and punishes the tests for mutants that could not even compile.

challenges.name: mutation-score-gate
challenges.title: Mutation score as the agent's quality gate
challenges.description:
CodeDev's agents may only open a pull request when the tests they wrote catch mistakes, not just run the code. The CI job records a mutation-testing run as JSON, and you write mutationReport(run), which turns it into a report and a pass/fail decision. Input: { "threshold": integer 0-100, "mutants": [{ "id": integer, "file": string, "line": integer, "mutator": string, "status": string }] }.

Statuses (the same definitions StrykerJS documents):
- detected = "killed" + "timeout"; undetected = "survived" + "no-coverage"; valid = detected + undetected.
- "compile-error" and "ignored" mutants are not valid: they count nowhere.
- Any other status (letter case matters): return { "error": "unknown status \"<status>\" for mutant <id>" } for the first such mutant in input order, and nothing else.

Score of a group of mutants: null when valid is 0, otherwise the percentage rounded half up to one decimal: Math.round(detected * 1000 / valid) / 10.

Return { files, overall, undetected, gate }:
- "files": one { "file", "detected", "valid", "score" } per file that has at least one mutant (any status), sorted by file name in code-unit order.
- "overall": { "detected", "valid", "score" } for all mutants.
- "undetected": one string "<file>:<line> <mutator> <status> #<id>" per survived or no-coverage mutant, sorted by file (code-unit order), then line, then id (both as numbers).
- "gate": "pass" when overall valid > 0 and the exact score, not the rounded one, is at least the threshold (detected / valid >= threshold / 100); otherwise "fail".

The test runner prints the returned object as JSON. A run has at most about 500 mutants.
hints: For each status, ask: did the tests notice this mutant, miss it, or tell us nothing about the tests at all? Which group does a timeout belong to, and which a compile error?

Count detected and valid with one helper, use it for each file and for the whole run, and compare the gate with whole numbers (detected * 100 against threshold * valid) instead of the rounded score. Check how your sort compares line 9 with line 12.

A similar run: 7 killed, 1 timeout, 2 survived, 1 no coverage and 3 compile errors gives detected 8 and valid 11, so the score is Math.round(8000 / 11) / 10 = 72.7. Against a threshold of 73 it fails, even though 72.7 would be shown as "73" with no decimals.
